key_insight: Genetic liability to adult internalizing–cardiometabolic multimorbidity is associated with early-life health changes and higher circulating inflammatory proteins.
clinical_relevance: These findings highlight potential early biological markers of shared mental and cardiometabolic disease liability, but do not establish clinical screening or treatment utility.
method: Analyzed 5,934 participants in the UK ALSPAC birth cohort.
Used mixed-effects models to assess associations between polygenic liability and trajectories of 12 mental and cardiometabolic outcomes.
Tested associations with circulating inflammatory proteins at ages 9 and 24 using the Olink Target 96 Inflammation panel.
evidence_signal: Higher polygenic liability was consistently associated with higher IL6, TNFSF14 and HGF levels at both ages 9 and 24.
watch_item: This observational cohort study does not establish causality or evaluate AI, cancer drug discovery, or clinical interventions.
paper_title: Early-life hallmarks of polygenic liability to adult internalizing-cardiometabolic multimorbidity
